name: How Do I Compare Kitchen Remodel Bids That Use Different Cabinet and Countertop Allowances?

mainEntity.name: Why are two San Diego kitchen renovation bids thousands apart when both contractors promise the same layout?
mainEntity.text: Why are two San Diego kitchen renovation bids thousands apart when both contractors promise the same layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two bids are not comparable unless they describe the same finished product. One contractor may include semi-custom cabinets, premium hardware, countertop installation, drywall repair, permits, and cleanup, while another may use low allowances and exclude those items. Create a comparison sheet with demolition, disposal, framing, plumbing, electrical, gas, ventilation, cabinets, hardware, countertops, backsplash, flooring, paint, appliances, permits, inspections, delivery, installation, cleanup, and warranty work. Record brand, model, quantity, dimensions, finish, and allowance for every major item. Ask each contractor to price the same plans and product schedule. Identify items that can increase after selection, including stone, tile, appliance panels, filler pieces, trim, and electrical upgrades. Ask how measurement errors, damaged materials, shortages, and delays are handled. Check whether the contractor has included countertop templating, cabinet scribing, floor leveling, and final connections. A bid with a higher fixed price may be safer than a low bid built around unrealistic allowances. Choose the proposal that is clearest, complete, and financially understandable rather than comparing only the headline total.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen bids can differ because contractors may use different cabinet grades, countertop allowances, labor assumptions, permit fees, appliance responsibilities, finish details, and exclusions. Compare identical plans and product specifications line by line, then separate fixed prices from allowances. The lowest total may not represent the lowest completed-project cost.
